heroLead: Focal Flow is the Hong Kong expense path: a photo of a ticket, government fares on MTR and bus, then a BPMN 2.0 case your managers can actually replay. In-house. On your CPU. No mystery cloud.
heroShotNeed: Record 15–25s from EventQR: claim screen → receipt extract overlay → fare map → BPMN canvas → instance replay. Save as /assets/focal-flow/hero.mp4 (1920×1080, silent loop).
proofTitle: Snap the ticket. Price the journey. Run the flow.
proofBody: Staff should not retype a lunch receipt, guess a Tsuen Wan fare, or lose an approval in email. Focal Flow keeps OCR, Hong Kong transit data, and a standard BPMN engine on the same case.
suiteLead: Each desk is useful on its own. Together they take a paper ticket to a signed, auditable instance.
suite0Blurb: In-house multimodal read in under 10s per receipt — or PaddleOCR, on your iron.
suite1Blurb: Daily MTR, KMB, and Citybus fares from government sources, not a spreadsheet.
suite2Blurb: No-code editor, BPMN 2.0, versioning, RBAC on every step, visual history replay.
ocrBody: Upload a photo. An in-house multimodal model extracts merchant, date, amount, and tax on a CPU — typically under ten seconds, at high accuracy. Batch queues run hands-free. Phone uploads use a one-time QR so the file never has to wander through chat.
ocrFeat0Body: Fully hosted intelligent multimodal model. No third-party vision API. Tuned for Hong Kong receipts on CPU hardware.
ocrFeat1Body: Drop a folder. The queue scans, retries, and parks exceptions without someone babysitting each file.
ocrFeat2Body: Choose AI OCR or traditional on-prem PaddleOCR per extraction pattern — same fields, different guts.
ocrFeat3Body: A short-lived QR lets the phone upload the receipt to the desktop case. No USB. No WhatsApp compression.
ocrAlt: Single receipt AI OCR extraction (media pending)
ocrNeed: Screenshot EventQR claim + BoundingBoxCanvas: one receipt, highlighted fields, elapsed time under 10s. Save as /assets/focal-flow/ocr-single.png (16:9, 1920×1080).
ocrBatchNeed: Screenshot the batch upload queue with several receipts in queued / scanning / done. Save as /assets/focal-flow/ocr-batch.png.
ocrEngineAlt: AI OCR vs PaddleOCR pattern picker (media pending)
ocrEngineNeed: Screenshot the extraction-pattern control showing AI OCR and local PaddleOCR (EventQR PaddleOcrTest + claim options). Save as /assets/focal-flow/ocr-engines.png.
ocrQrNeed: Record 8–15s: desktop shows one-time QR → phone camera → receipt lands on the claim. EventQR QRGenerator + MobileReceiptUpload. Save as /assets/focal-flow/ocr-qr.mp4.
transitTitle: Fares that match what the government published today.
transitBody: The calculator is not a static table. MTR and bus (KMB, Citybus) fares refresh from official datasources on a daily cadence, so a Tsuen Wan to Admiralty claim prices the same way the gate does.
transitFeat0Body: Transit data is pulled from government sources and refreshed daily — not typed into a spreadsheet once a year.
transitFeat1Body: MTR plus KMB and Citybus in one calculator, so a mixed journey is one fare line on the case.
transitAlt: Fare calculator with MTR and bus (media pending)
transitNeed: Screenshot EventQR FareCalculator: origin, destination, MTR line colours, a KMB or Citybus hop, and the fare. Save as /assets/focal-flow/transit-calculator.png.
transitMapNeed: Screenshot TransitMap / MtrNetworkMap (and BusRouteMap if a bus leg is selected). Save as /assets/focal-flow/transit-map.png.
bpmnTitle: A flow you can draw, ship, and rewind.
bpmnBody: Designers drag a standard BPMN 2.0 diagram — not a proprietary spaghetti. Version it, revert it, hang RBAC on every step, then replay any instance as if you were in the room.
bpmnFeat0Body: Configurable drag-and-drop editor. Business owners change the path without a deploy ticket.
bpmnFeat1Body: The definition is Business Process Model and Notation 2.0. Take it to another engine or another environment without a rewrite.
bpmnFeat2Body: Every published flow keeps a history. Roll back a bad path the way you roll back a document.
bpmnFeat3Body: Standard role-based access on actions and steps — manager, accountant, clerk — not a single god-mode inbox.
bpmnFeat4Body: Every instance can be replayed visually, step by step, so audit is a film, not a log dump.
bpmnNeed: Record 12–20s of the no-code editor: drag a user task, connect a gateway, save. Prefer Flowable / EventQR process designer. Save as /assets/focal-flow/bpmn-editor.mp4.
bpmnXmlNeed: Screenshot the BPMN 2.0 diagram or XML export (EventQR flowable-files / reimbursementProcess). Save as /assets/focal-flow/bpmn-xml.png.
bpmnVerNeed: Screenshot version list + revert for a workflow definition. Save as /assets/focal-flow/bpmn-versions.png.
bpmnRbacNeed: Screenshot a step with roles (manager vs accountant forms in EventQR). Save as /assets/focal-flow/bpmn-rbac.png.
bpmnReplayNeed: Record 10–20s of WorkflowHistoryLandscape: play an instance step by step with the token moving. Save as /assets/focal-flow/bpmn-replay.mp4.
ctaTitle: Ready for expenses that do not live in email?
ctaSubtitle: We will walk OCR, Hong Kong fares, and a BPMN case against your programme — then show how enquiry lands with FDS.
roomBookingTitle: Scan the wall. Unlock the room.
roomBookingBody: Interactive floor plan, a five-digit door code, a QR sticker. Same idea as reimbursement — the real world starts it, Focal Flow finishes it.
